tagline: Four miles through a town that quarried bridge granite.
intro: Route 67 comes over the Bridgewater line and runs a little under four miles east into Roxbury, a town settled about 1713 whose old name, Shepaug, is a Mahican word for rocky water. At the town center Route 317 turns north up Church Street past the Congregational church, and the scenic part ends at Painter Hill Road, where the street becomes Good Hill Road.

Mine Hill, in the northwest of town, was dug for gold, silver and lead in the 1700s. None of it lasted more than a few years. The iron turned out to be the real thing, and the granite quarried there went into the Brooklyn Bridge and Grand Central Terminal.

moments.title: Mine Hills Preserve
moments.text: Trails run along the east face of Mine Hill past old quarries to the stone blast furnaces of an ironworks that closed in 1905, with panels explaining what each part was for.

moments.title: Roxbury Center
moments.text: Route 317 leaves Route 67 in the town center and goes up Church Street past Roxbury Congregational Church, inside a historic district of 32 buildings.
